precedence: 1. Brand constraints marked non_negotiable: absolute, always blocking.
2. Brand overrides: replace the targeted KB rule within the entry's scope. The KB text is kept as the default in every decision log entry.
3. KB rules activated for the deck profile.
4. Brand constraints and advisories: add requirements. 'tighten' keeps the KB rule and adds the brand condition. 'reinforce' raises the KB rule's severity to blocking.
5. Brand entries marked 'kb_retained': the brand and KB disagree and the KB wins. Logged so the brand owner can promote it to an override.

scope: tells you what your data means

verbatim.positioning: For early-stage biotech and pharma R&D teams who must report progress to boards, investors, and executives, Helix Bioworks is a data layer that turns a lab's own research and trial data into a board-ready update in minutes. Unlike manual reporting or general-purpose AI writing tools, Helix Brief works directly from the lab's own data and flags what a non-scientist reader actually needs to know, rather than producing a generic summary or a plausible-sounding paraphrase.

entries.rule: Never state a clinical, scientific, or performance outcome the underlying data does not support, however well the claim would land.
entries.check: Every outcome claim traces to a named evidence item whose stated result supports it at the stated certainty.

entries.rule: Never use hype language anywhere in the deck, notes, or appendix.
entries.check: No term from the banned vocabulary list appears in any text field.

entries.rule: Never imply more certainty than the evidence earns. When the honest answer is 'we don't know yet', state the gap plainly rather than trimming the uncertain material out.
entries.check: Preliminary findings are labeled preliminary. Known gaps appear as stated gaps, on the slide where the related claim appears.

targets.note: AUD-16 allows minimizing speculation for funders. The brand requires flagging it instead, never silently removing it.

entries.rule: Human judgment stays in the loop for anything investor-facing. No deck is marked final while any tool decision in its log is unreviewed.
entries.check: If the spec status is 'final', every decision log entry has a review verdict.

entries.rule: Never claim validation, adoption, or traction without a specific number and a named basis (for example, the design partner cohort).
entries.check: Evidence tagged adoption or traction contains a numeral and a source.

entries.source: §2.3 Respect for the reader's time, §8.2 Reader-first sequencing
entries.rule: State the point before the context at every level. Do not withhold a resolution for dramatic effect.
entries.check: Each section opens with its conclusion. No section is built as a reveal.

targets.replacement: Present the current state before the proposed state for contrast, but state the resolution immediately. The delayed-resolution variant for inspiration is not used.

targets.note: Skeptical audiences may get supporting evidence before a section's recommendation, but the deck thesis still appears in the executive summary.
Surface the contrary assumption in one sentence at most, then the evidence, then the assertion.

entries.source: §2.1 Scientific integrity over polish, §6.3 Old way, new way
entries.rule: Present data in the order it occurred, and frame stakes by the real cost of the current process. No rhetorical sequencing, invented urgency, or villain.
entries.check: Figures appear in chronological or logical order, not reordered for contrast. Stakes cite the actual cost of the manual process.

targets.replacement: Show trend data in the order it occurred. Do not reorder figures to sharpen a sense of improvement.
Frame stakes as the concrete, current cost of the old process (days of research-associate time, drift between data and board update). Do not frame by fear of loss or invented urgency.

entries.rule: Do not borrow authority. Category-level momentum, competitor funding, or general industry statistics are never evidence about Helix Bioworks. Cite Helix's own cohort by name and number.
entries.check: No evidence item uses an external authority or market statistic as a proxy for Helix validation.

targets.replacement: Back claims about Helix with Helix's own named, numbered evidence. External authorities may support claims about the market or the problem, never as proxy validation of Helix.

entries.source: §9.4 Investor updates ('zero persuasive technique'), §8.3 Restraint as signal
entries.rule: Prefer the precise, sourced figure. Narrative and human-interest material may only illustrate a sourced figure, never stand in for one or win a tie on resonance.
entries.check: Where an anecdote or story appears, it sits beside the figure it illustrates and is never the primary evidence.

targets.replacement: When evidence is of equal strength, prefer the more precise and better-sourced item. Surface a surprising sourced finding as the headline.
Engage through clarity and evidence. Emotional appeal is limited to the concrete cost of the old process as described in the brand's old-way/new-way framing.

targets.note: The memorable moment must be a sourced figure or real product output, not a story or evocative image.

entries.source: §8 Voice mission ('a careful scientist talking to a colleague they respect'), §9.4 tone modifiers
entries.rule: No humor in investor, collateral, PR, website, or advertising material.
entries.check: No jokes, puns, or humorous asides on slides or in notes.

targets.replacement: Do not use humor. Metaphor is allowed only where it clarifies a mechanism and is drawn from the audience's own working context.

targets.note: The opening hook is a sourced fact or the old-way/new-way contrast. Stories and challenges to conventional wisdom are not used as hooks.

entries.rule: Speaker notes stay in the brand voice: plain, specific, active voice, conversational but never casual. No rhetorical questions, exclamation points, or intensifiers.
entries.check: Notes read like a careful scientist briefing a colleague.

targets.note: Conversational is fine. Casual, salesy, or enthusiastic is not.
Engagement prompts in notes are optional for investor decks and must not be rhetorical.

entries.source: §6.3 Old way, new way ('The contrast is the argument')
entries.rule: Use the old-way/new-way contrast as the deck's central argument device. Section dividers may carry a short question as an eyebrow, but every content headline is a declarative assertion.
entries.check: The deck contains an explicit before/after contrast slide. No content headline is phrased as a question.

entries.rule: No exclamation points, em dashes, en dashes used as dashes, or semicolons in any text.
entries.check: Punctuation scan finds none.

entries.rule: 'Helix Bioworks' on first reference, 'Helix' acceptable after. Never 'HB'. 'Helix Brief' always in full. 'The Helix platform' never abbreviated.
entries.check: First company mention in reading order is 'Helix Bioworks'. No 'HB'.

entries.rule: Never describe Helix as 'an AI tool', 'an AI writing platform', or 'a reporting dashboard'. The category is 'the data layer between the bench and the boardroom'.
entries.check: No self-description uses the avoided category terms.

entries.source: §6.1 North Star positioning ('does not get paraphrased in formal usage ... pitch decks')
entries.rule: The positioning statement appears verbatim in pitch decks, on the positioning slide.
entries.check: The positioning slide body matches the North Star statement exactly.

targets.note: The verbatim statement runs past the 30-word live body target. The positioning slide is exempt from the word cap in both variants.

entries.rule: Every performance claim names its basis: time savings cite the cohort, cost claims state the comparison basis, risk claims name the specific failure mode, comparisons describe the manual process accurately.
entries.check: Evidence tagged time_savings, cost, risk, or comparative carries the field its category requires.

entries.rule: Claims about a customer's scientific results must carry their stage and stay within what that stage permits.
entries.check: Customer-result evidence has a stage. Active-trial evidence makes no outcome claim. Unpublished results are customer-approved.

entries.rule: A partner-named result requires the partner's explicit approval. Unapproved figures are anonymized. A partner logo is never larger than or dominant over the Helix Bioworks mark.
entries.check: Partner-named evidence has approval recorded.

entries.rule: Helix Brief structures data. It never interprets results. No copy may say or imply that it tells a reader what data means.
entries.check: No claim attributes interpretation or judgment to the product.

entries.rule: Seed the objection pass with the brand's investor objections: 'isn't this just another AI tool', 'what stops a portfolio company building this', and data-handling questions. Data-handling objections need a specific current answer or are escalated, never answered with reassurance.
entries.check: The alternatives/objections content addresses each listed investor objection or records why not.

entries.rule: Position against the manual process, and against tools not tied to source data. Never compare on writing quality.
entries.check: Competitive comparisons turn on data grounding and traceability.

entries.rule: Headlines in Tiempos Headline, body and labels in Inter, data values in IBM Plex Mono. Never Tiempos for body text.
entries.check: Rendered text uses the role-correct typeface.

targets.replacement: Use the brand type system: serif (Tiempos Headline) for headlines only at 28pt or larger, sans-serif (Inter) for all body, label, and chart text, monospace (IBM Plex Mono) for data values. Three families total, each restricted to its role.

entries.rule: Brand sizes are specified for web (H1 40px, body 16px). For projected slides, the KB legibility floor governs and the brand ramp is scaled up.
entries.check: Live slides meet DSN-26 minimums. Read variant may use the brand ramp scaled to page size.

targets.note: Brand web sizes would fall below the projection floor. KB wins. Promote to an override only if the brand owner specifies slide sizes.

entries.rule: Chart color: Ink Navy for the proof series, Mist for context series, Ochre for one flagged point at most per chart, Signal Teal only for positive indicators. Ochre never carries text.
entries.check: At most one Ochre element per chart. No Ochre text.

targets.replacement: Render the series that proves the claim in Ink Navy, everything else in Mist, and mark at most one flagged point in Ochre.

targets.note: Palette fixed to the brand set.

entries.rule: Line for trends, bar for comparisons, never 3D or dual-axis, pies limited to three segments.
entries.check: Chart specs comply.

targets.note: KB allows up to eight slices when a pie is used. Brand allows three. DAT-09 still discourages pies whenever comparison matters.

entries.rule: Imagery shows real lab environments with practical light. Never the glowing DNA helix, blue-gloved-hands stock, double helix icon, or flask icon.
entries.check: No image or icon carries a banned subject tag.

entries.rule: Logo clear space equals the cap height of the H. Minimum 24px digital. No rotation, shadow, or recolor.
entries.check: Logo placements respect clear space and size.

entries.rule: Executive summary order: headline finding, supporting data, what changed since the last conversation, what is still open.
entries.check: The executive summary includes a 'still open' line.

entries.rule: One core proof point per page, data-forward, minimal decoration.
entries.check: No content slide carries more than one primary proof point.

entries.rule: State the ask plainly. No urgency devices ('limited', 'don't miss', 'act now') and no conversion CTA language.
entries.check: Closing slide states the ask without urgency phrasing.

entries.rule: Never follow a figure with an intensifier or enthusiasm marker.
entries.check: No intensifier list term appears in any text.

entries.rule: Use numerals for any figure that is or could be a data point, including under ten.
entries.check: Spelled-out numbers attached to units or counts are flagged.
entries.brand_doc_conflict: §8.1 and §9.6 use 'three design partners' as on-brand examples, which contradicts this rule. Advisory until the brand owner resolves it.

entries.rule: Charts never rely on color alone. Every image carries descriptive alt text.
entries.check: Images have alt text. Charts with more than one series use labels, not color only.

targets.note: Direct labels or patterns so meaning never depends on color alone.
